subject: general
question: If the calliper bore diameter worn is greater than 2.630 inches (66.80 mm), what corrective action is recommended?
solution:
The correct answer is __Replacing the calliper housing**(Option 1)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Calliper bore diameter wear__ can affect the efficiency of the braking system.
 
• If the bore diameter exceeds 2.630 inches (66.80 mm), it may lead to improper sealing and brake fluid leakage.
 
• Replacing the calliper housing ensures optimal brake performance and safety.
 
• Other options like replacing the piston or tightening the inlet fitting will not resolve the issue caused by an oversized bore diameter.
 
• Maintaining the correct bore diameter is essential for the longevity and reliability of the brake system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Brake System Maintenance:**

 
 
• Routine inspections are crucial to ensure components are within specifications.
 
• Timely replacement of worn parts prevents accidents and failures.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Correct Bore Diameter:**
 
 
• The bore diameter directly affects hydraulic pressure within the braking system.
 
• Maintaining the specified diameter ensures efficient brake application.
 
 
 
• **Other Components to Inspect:**
 
 
• Brake pads, rotors, and brake lines should also be regularly checked.
 
• Ensure proper lubrication and fluid levels in the system.
